checkpoints: A dangling node in PageRank is one with out-degree zero — it has no outlinks at all, so under the bare recurrence its rank mass has nowhere to flow.

In this loop, the inner accumulation `for (const v of inLinks.get(u) ?? [])` only gathers rank FROM other nodes' inlinks; there is no separate step anywhere that collects a dangling node's rank and redistributes it back across the graph.

Because dangling mass is never redistributed, the sum of the `rank` map drifts below 1 after every pass of the `for (let it = 0; it < MAX_ITERATIONS; it++)` loop, and the resulting rank ordering becomes unstable across iterations.

The fix is to compute, each iteration before building `newRank`, a `danglingSum` equal to the sum of `rank.get(u)` over every node whose `outDegree` is zero, then derive `danglingShare = (DAMPING * danglingSum) / N` and add that share to every node alongside the existing `teleport = (1 - DAMPING) / N` term so the rank vector re-normalizes to sum to 1.

This bug is dangerous precisely because the code still runs to completion and returns superficially plausible numbers; the decay only becomes visible on a real corpus containing dead-end pages, which is why it slips past shallow or toy-graph tests.

In code review, the tell is structural rather than a runtime error: there is no variable resembling `danglingSum` or `danglingShare` anywhere near the main iteration loop, signaling the redistribution step was simply never written.

A regression test for this class of bug should assert that `[...rank.values()].reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)` stays approximately 1 after every single iteration, run against a graph that deliberately includes at least one dangling node so the faulty path is actually exercised.

The missing correction is conceptually the same kind of uniform redistribution as the teleport term — both `teleport` and `danglingShare` add a flat amount to every node per iteration, so omitting the dangling term is easy to overlook since the code superficially resembles a correct damped power-iteration implementation.
